My entire company is run on Linux, mostly Ubuntu, some Debian. All of the standard office programs. We use Money Manager -- it's a fantastic accounting system -- for bookkeeping. Gimp for image editing. We use ejabberd for in-office IM. We also use an open-source medical records program. It was free, instead of paying $10,000+ for one that didn't work as well and was less secure. There is one laptop in the building that runs Windows, because it uses a vendor-supplied program that, because of driver issues, cannot run under WINE or in a VM. That laptop is kept in isolation because of the security issues inherent in using Windows. It can't internet and it can't talk to anyone else.

Unrelated, but important: In the medical field, security is a joke. Trust me, your doctor's records are about as secure as a roll of toilet paper. I've had trouble accessing online services (labs, radiology), because they only support IE. When I ask them why, they say "security," and I laugh my ass off. Password requirements are a joke. Four-character passwords are the norm, but you have to change them every 6 months, for "security." Want to get into any lab in the country? Call a primary care doctor's office (they are almost all owned by either a hospital or a corporation), tell the front desk that you're from IT at SuperLabs, there's a problem with their account, and you are going to change their password, and get their password, log in boom. You're looking at the results for Aunt Sophie's HIV test after her trip to Puerto Vallarta last year.

I use Xubuntu as my OS. I use Blender for editing photos, videos and making CG. It's an amazing program, basically a graphics swiss army knife. It's very powerful. For simple graphics editing though, I use GIMP which is really wonderful, really fast and powerful as well. For browsing, I use Pale Moon which is a fork of Firefox optimized for speed and privacy. My office suite is OpenOffice. It's fast and has great features. It's compatible with MS Office files, like LibreOffice. People say LibreOffice is a bit better but I prefer OpenOffice. My torrent client is qBittorrent, which is a great alternative to uTorrent (don't use that crap, it's adware and it's affiliated to the MPAA). It's fast, reliable and lightweight. I use a lot more FLOSS stuff, but these are the ones I think deserve to be known.
